reference_summary: At 14:03:17.250, Synthetic Helios Ridge point-of-interconnection voltage fell from 0.98 per unit to 0.72 per unit within 92 milliseconds. Primary cause was the Synthetic Helios Ridge central controller's reactive current command timeout of 60 milliseconds, which expired during the voltage depression. Because the command timeout expired, reactive current stayed at 0.12 per unit for 60 milliseconds before rising to 0.45 per unit. Voltage support fell short by 0.33 per unit reactive current for 60 milliseconds, delaying recovery but not causing a voltage collapse. After the event, Synthetic Helios Ridge increased the reactive current command timeout from 60 milliseconds to 140 milliseconds to cover communication jitter.
title: Synthetic Helios Ridge Inverter Ride-Through Response to Fictional Voltage Depression

reference_summary: At 09:17:22.100, Synthetic Borealis Solar Station terminal voltage dropped from 0.97 per unit to 0.68 per unit in 75 milliseconds. Primary cause was the reactive current limiter setting of 0.30 per unit in inverter group three, lower than the required 0.45 per unit. The reactive current limiter clamped actual injection at 0.30 per unit, even though the controller reference indicated 0.45 per unit. Reactive current shortfall was 0.15 per unit for 520 milliseconds, reducing voltage support compared with the required characteristic. After the event, engineers corrected the inverter group three limiter setting from 0.30 per unit to 0.45 per unit.

reference_summary: By 2026-09-12T14:00Z Synthetic Larkspur engineers corrected the LMT-1 auxiliary contact wiring and added independent voltage verification before automated sectionalizer closure. At 2026-09-11T02:14:00Z a tree branch contacted Synthetic Larkspur Feeder LK-11, drawing 4.8 kA fault current measured by an independent line relay. At 2026-09-11T02:15:10Z R-LK11 completed three trip operations and entered recloser lockout, leaving 1,850 customers without power on LK-11. The primary cause was a miswired LMT-1 auxiliary contact that reported open while the tie switch was actually closed during storm restoration. At 03:07:40Z the restoration script closed AS-L3 and then AS-L7 based on the false open indication from LMT-1, forming a closed loop. The trip de-energized 1,850 customers for 47 minutes until manual switching restored sections between 03:54Z and 04:01Z.
title: Synthetic Larkspur Feeder Loop Restoration Miscoordination During Synthetic Storm Cell 20260911

reference_summary: By 2026-09-13T09:00Z Synthetic Juniper engineers corrected the restoration script to open JWT-2 before closing any automated sectionalizer on JN-08. Recloser R-JN08 tripped at 04:22:10.5Z, reclosed at 04:22:15Z, and tripped again at 04:22:16Z on the persistent fault. At 2026-09-11T04:22:50Z R-JN08 entered recloser lockout after three trip operations, interrupting service to 2,100 customers on JN-08. The primary cause was the restoration script closing AS-J4 and AS-J9 before opening tie switch JWT-2, creating a parallel path between sources. At 05:12:20Z the restoration script closed AS-J4 then AS-J9 while JWT-2 remained closed, forming a loop between Juniper and Willow sources. The trip de-energized 2,100 customers for 52 minutes until manual switching restored sections between 06:04Z and 06:12Z.

reference_summary: At 14:03:10 on 2026-09-11, Synthetic Riverside Substation bus A held 13.8 kV while bus B measured 13.7 kV. At 14:04:22, the control room initiated a bus transfer from source A to source B using the automated transfer scheme. A maintenance tag on tie breaker B-12A incorrectly recorded the tie as normally closed, misdirecting transfer logic. The phase overcurrent element timed out after 0.12 seconds and issued a trip to tie breaker B-12A. The synthetic water treatment plant lost motor supply for seven minutes, though no equipment damage was calculated. At 14:11:32, operators re-energized bus A from source A after verifying tie breaker B-12A was open.
title: Synthetic Riverside Bus Transfer Maintenance Tag Mismatch Incident

reference_summary: At 09:12:05 on 2026-09-11, Synthetic North Harbor Substation operated with bus X at 69 kV and bus Y at 69.3 kV. A maintenance tag on disconnector D-7 incorrectly listed bus Y as de-energized, so transfer logic treated the alternate feed as safe. At 09:13:42, the transfer controller issued a close command to bus tie breaker T-3 based on the mismatched tag. The definite-time overcurrent element tripped bus tie breaker T-3 after 0.20 seconds at 09:13:42.550. The synthetic packaging line stopped for eleven minutes, and no damage calculation exceeded the one-hour rated thermal limit. Maintenance updated the tag database at 10:05:00 to require voltage confirmation before any automatic bus transfer.
title: Synthetic North Harbor Bus Transfer Tag Ambiguity Incident
